sentences.text: Heard on I.A.No.9376/2024, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant-Dinesh @ Dumman.

Appellant - Dinesh @ Dumman, is aggrieved of the judgment dated 07.10.2023, passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, II Additional Sessions Judge, Damoh (M.P.), in Special Trial No.07/2023, whereby, the present appellant has been convicted with co-accused Pradeep @ Ranu for offence punishable under Section 342 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for one year with fine of Rs.500/- with default stipulation of 15 days additional imprisonment, under Section 376(D)(A) of IPC, he sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- and default stipulation of 6 months additional imprisonment, respectively.
It is submitted that appellant is innocent.

entities.text: POCSO Act, II Additional Sessions Judge, Damoh (M.P.)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The only allegation is that his house was used by the main accused Pradeep @ Ranu.
There are no overt or covert act attributed to the present appellant.

He has already remained in custody for 277 days during the trial and he is in custody since 07.10.2023,
when judgment was passed.
There are good chances of success in appeal.
Police has not seized the CCTV footage to show the presence of the present appellant, though CCTV cameras were installed in his house.
There is no criminal antecedent against the present appellant.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to 2 CRA-15243-2023 the appellant-Dinesh @ Dumman.
Shri Puneet Shroti, learned Govt. Advocate strongly opposes the prayer of the appellant.

Taking these facts into consideration, the fact of incarceration as also the fact that Police has not seized the CCTV footage to show the presence of the present appellant, though CCTV cameras were installed in his house, no overt or covert act attributed to the present appellant, there is no criminal antecedent against the appellant, it is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Dinesh @ Dumman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10728135/
1 Only)

Dumman shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (DEVN  JUDGE   A.Praj.
